claim.statement: GitLab's current security documentation describes remote flows as using runner execution with composite identity, sandbox and network controls, flow-defined tool restrictions, server-side tool-response sanitization and prompt-injection detection, while stating that human-in-the-loop approval is not applied to flows.

source.title: Security threats in agentic systems
source.locator: Content protection layers and execution-mode security-control table

values: user-managed runner configured for secure execution

limitations: These are publisher-described controls and threat-model boundaries, not independent penetration-test or execution receipts.
The separate execution documentation makes sandbox availability conditional on an SRT-compatible image and privileged runner configuration; custom non-SRT and hardened UBI images are excluded.
unknowns: Which controls were enabled, effective and correctly enforced in any execution are unknown.
Control versions, detection thresholds, sanitizer behavior, allowed destinations and residual risks were not independently evaluated.

relationships.note: The security architecture describes the secure remote-flow mode; runner documentation shows that the sandbox depends on image and privileged-runner configuration.
